mainTopic: Long gaps between a birth and its שליא or a twin, and whether a שליא in a house makes it טמא
overview: The amud opens with the end of a ברייתא that suspects two births when a fetus and a שליא come out together. The גמרא calls it a תיובתא against the earlier claim. Next come reports of real cases about how long a שליא or a second twin can come after a birth: ten days (שמואל), twenty-three days (רבי יוחנן), and thirty-three days for a twin (רבי יצחק), with רב יוסף correcting the numbers by one day. A question about the 34-day twin gap is answered by swapping the numbers, so 33 days was about a שליא and 23 days was about a twin. Then a report of twins born three months apart, the sons of רבי חייא, is explained by אביי as one drop that split in two. The גמרא then turns to the משנה's rule that a שליא in a house makes the house טמא. רבי מאיר holds there is always a baby with it, and three sages disagree. רב פפא explains רבי שמעון's reason as a rule that mixed טומאה is בטל, and teaches not to stay silent before one's teacher. Finally, רבה reports and challenges the study hall's explanation of רבי שמעון's view on a ladleful of רקב mixed with dirt, and his challenge continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The ברייתא ends: suspect two births
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא closes by ruling that the woman keeps the stringencies of two births. It explains that perhaps one sac and one שליא both dissolved.
steps.simpleTranslation: She keeps the stricter rules of having given birth to two babies. For I say: maybe the sac belonging to the afterbirth dissolved, and the afterbirth belonging to the sac dissolved.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the quote of a ברייתא that is being used to challenge an earlier opinion. The ברייתא says we must worry there were two separate babies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The woman discharged a fetus shaped like an animal, and she also discharged a שליא. The ברייתא does not simply assume the שליא belonged to that fetus. It suggests that one baby's sac dissolved and the other baby's שליא dissolved, so each item could come from a different baby. Because one might be a boy and one a girl, she keeps the stricter rules of both.

keyTerms.meaning: Stringency; the stricter side of the rules
The fluid-filled sac surrounding a fetus

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read this as saying the שליא and the sac belong to the same baby. The point is the opposite: each part may come from a different baby, and the matching part of each one dissolved.

phrases.english: the stringency of two offspring,
phrases.notes: This is the end of a sentence that began before this section: she keeps the strict rules as if she had two babies.

phrases.english: for I say: perhaps
the sac of the afterbirth dissolved
and the afterbirth of the sac dissolved.
phrases.notes: In other words, the baby that came with the שליא lost its sac, and the baby that came in a sac lost its שליא.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁאֲנִי אוֹמֵר שֶׁמָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא quoted before this section.
steps.kashyaTarget: The earlier claim that a שליא cannot be tied to a fetus of this kind
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא openly considers this kind of fetus and a שליא together, showing it treats such a link as possible.

steps.title: The challenge stands as a refutation
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא declares the ברייתא a conclusive refutation of the earlier claim.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is a refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rules that the challenge from the ברייתא cannot be answered. The earlier claim is knocked down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No answer is offered to defend the earlier opinion. The single word תיובתא closes the discussion and shows the ברייתא wins.

keyTerms.meaning: A conclusive refutation; the challenge cannot be answered

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא proved the earlier claim wrong, and the גמרא accepts the refutation without any answer.

phrases.english: A refutation.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּיוּבְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rules on the challenge from step 1.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The earlier claim is refuted by the ברייתא.

steps.title: שמואל: afterbirth linked to a baby ten days earlier
steps.stepSummary: שמואל reports a real case where the שליא was linked to a baby born up to ten days before. He adds that we link it only when the שליא comes out after the baby.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר שילא said in the name of רב מתנה, in the name of שמואל: there was a case where they linked the afterbirth to the baby, up to ten days later. And they only said we link it when the afterbirth comes after the baby.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic starts. שמואל tells of a real case showing how long after a birth a שליא can still be linked to that baby.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the שליא is linked to the earlier baby, there is no need to worry that it came with another unseen baby. שמואל sets a gap of up to ten days. He also limits the rule: it applies only when the שליא comes out after the baby, not before it.

keyTerms.meaning: We attribute or link (one thing to another)
That comes out after the baby

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a series of reports about how long a gap can still count as one birth. The next steps give longer numbers.

phrases.english: Rabba bar Sheila said,
Rav Mattana said, Shmuel said:
There was a case and they attributed the afterbirth to the baby
up to ten days,
and they only said that we attribute
in the case of an afterbirth that comes after the baby.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר שֵׁילָא אָמַר רַב מַתְנָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל מַעֲשֶׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new set of reports after the refutation ended the previous discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שליא may be linked to a baby born up to ten days earlier, but only if it comes out after the baby.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: a twenty-three day gap
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן reports a case where the שליא was linked to a baby born up to twenty-three days earlier.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: there was a case where they linked the afterbirth to the baby, up to twenty-three days later.
steps.whatsHappening: A second report gives a much longer gap than שמואל's ten days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is the same kind as שמואל's: a שליא linked to a baby already born. The only new information is the number. Here the gap is twenty-three days.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חַנָּה, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Ḥana said, Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
There was a case and they attributed the afterbirth to the baby,
up to twenty-three days.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חַנָּה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מַעֲשֶׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel report with a longer gap than step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שליא was linked to a baby born up to twenty-three days earlier.

steps.title: רב יוסף corrects the number to twenty-four
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף corrects the report: on another occasion, the speaker had told them twenty-four days.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said to him: you told us twenty-four.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף fixes the number in the report just given. He remembers hearing twenty-four days, not twenty-three.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not an argument about the law. It is a correction of the reported fact, changing the gap from twenty-three days to twenty-four.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said to him:
You told us up to twenty-four.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב יוֹסֵף עַד עֶשְׂרִים וְאַרְבָּעָה אָמְרַתְּ לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Corrects the number reported in step 4.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the exact number of days in the report
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The report said twenty-three days, but the earlier version had twenty-four.

steps.title: רבי יצחק: a twin born thirty-three days later
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק reports a case where the second twin stayed in the womb thirty-three days after the first was born.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא son of רב עוירא said in the name of רבי יצחק: there was a case where one baby stayed behind thirty-three days after the other.
steps.whatsHappening: A third report moves from the שליא to a second baby. One twin was born thirty-three days after the first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier reports showed a שליא coming out long after a birth. This report shows that even a whole second baby can come long after the first. That makes long gaps between parts of one pregnancy believable.

keyTerms.meaning: Its fellow, meaning the other twin

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב עַוִּירָא,
phrases.english: Rav Aḥa son of Rav Avira said,
Rabbi Yitzḥak said:
There was a case and a baby remained behind after its fellow
thirty-three days.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב עַוִּירָא אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק מַעֲשֶׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a report about a delayed second baby, continuing the theme of long gaps.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A twin was born thirty-three days after the first twin.

steps.title: רב יוסף corrects the number to thirty-four
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף again corrects the number: he had been told thirty-four days.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said to him: you told us thirty-four.
steps.whatsHappening: Just as in step 5, רב יוסף fixes the number of days in the report.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pattern repeats: each time, רב יוסף remembers the number as one day more than the report. Here thirty-three becomes thirty-four.
steps.whatToRemember: So far the reports are: ten days (שמואל), twenty-three or twenty-four days for a שליא (רבי יוחנן), and thirty-three or thirty-four days for a delayed twin (רבי יצחק). רב יוסף corrected both later numbers up by one day. Step 9 swaps which number belongs to the שליא and which to the twin.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said to him:
You told us thirty-four.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב יוֹסֵף שְׁלֹשִׁים וְאַרְבָּעָה אָמְרַתְּ לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Corrects the number reported in step 6, following the same pattern as step 5.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the exact number of days in the report
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The report said thirty-three days, but the earlier version had thirty-four.

steps.title: How can twins be born 34 days apart?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how a 34-day gap between twins is possible according to the view that a ninth-month baby is never born early.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works for the view that a ninth-month baby can be born before the ninth month is complete. Then one twin's form finished at the end of the seventh month, and the other's at the start of the ninth. But according to the view that a ninth-month baby is never born early, what can we say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the report from the last step that one twin stayed in the womb 34 days after the other. It shows how the gap works for one view, then asks how it could work for the other view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Babies are born either at the end of the seventh month or in the ninth month. If a ninth-month baby can come at the start of the ninth month, then end-of-seven to start-of-nine is about 34 days. If ninth-month babies come only at the end of the ninth month, the shortest gap is about two months, so a 34-day gap seems impossible.

keyTerms.meaning: This works out well (for one view). It is often the first half of a challenge.
Incomplete months, meaning born before the ninth month is fully over
His form was completed, meaning the baby was fully formed and ready to be born
What is there to say? A sign that the challenge has no easy answer

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not whether twins can be born at different times. Both sides accept that. The only problem is the exact number of 34 days, according to one view about ninth-month births.

phrases.english: This works out well according to the one who says
a woman who gives birth in the ninth month can give birth in incomplete months
phrases.notes: He means the ninth-month baby can arrive before the ninth month is fully over.

phrases.english: you can find such a case
one whose form was completed at the end of the seventh month
and one whose form was completed at the beginning of the ninth month.
But according to the one who says
a woman who gives birth in the ninth month cannot give birth in incomplete months
what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the 34-day twin gap reported in steps 6-7
steps.kashyaTarget: The report that one twin stayed in the womb 33 or 34 days after the other
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If ninth-month babies are born only at the end of the ninth month, twins born in the seventh and ninth months must be about two months apart, not 34 days.

steps.title: Swap the two numbers
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the numbers were switched: 33 days was about a שליא, and 23 days was about a twin.
steps.simpleTranslation: Reverse the teachings: thirty-three days was about the afterbirth, and twenty-three days was about the baby.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by saying the reports were mixed up. The longer number goes with the שליא, and the shorter number goes with the twin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's 23 days had been about a שליא, and רבי יצחק's 33 days had been about a twin. Swapping them means the twin gap is only 23 days. That is short enough not to need the idea of a ninth-month baby born early, so the problem goes away.

phrases.english: Reverse the teachings:
phrases.notes: He means the numbers from steps 4 and 6, רבי יוחנן's 23 days and רבי יצחק's 33 days.

phrases.english: thirty-three days was about the afterbirth
twenty-three days was about the baby.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיפוֹךְ שְׁמַעְתָּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 8
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 33 or 34 days was the gap between twins
steps.terutzMaskana: 33 days was about a שליא; the twin gap was 23 days

steps.title: Twins born three months apart: the sons of רבי חייא
steps.stepSummary: רב מנחם reports that one twin stayed in the womb three months after the other: יהודה and חזקיה, the sons of רבי חייא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבין בר רב אדא said in the name of רב מנחם of כפר שערים (some say בית שערים): It once happened that one baby stayed in the womb three months after the other. They are sitting before us in the בית המדרש. Who are they? יהודה and חזקיה, the sons of רבי חייא.
steps.whatsHappening: A new report gives a much longer gap between twins: three whole months. It names real people everyone knew as proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This goes far beyond the 23 or 34 days from earlier. Pointing to well-known people sitting in the בית המדרש makes the report hard to doubt. This sets up the next question about how such a long gap is possible.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אָבִין בַּר רַב אַדָּא,
phrases.english: Rabbi Avin bar Rav Adda said

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב מְנַחֵם אִישׁ כְּפַר שְׁעָרִים,
phrases.english: Rav Menachem of the village of She'arim said
and some say he was from Beit She'arim:
It once happened that one baby stayed in the womb
after the other one, for three months

phrases.aramaic: וַהֲרֵי הֵם יוֹשְׁבִים לְפָנֵינוּ בְּבֵית הַמִּדְרָשׁ.
phrases.english: and they are sitting before us in the study hall.
And who are they?
Yehuda and Chizkiya, the sons of Rabbi Chiya.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אָבִין בַּר רַב אַדָּא, אָמַר רַב מְנַחֵם אִישׁ כְּפַר שְׁעָרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another report about a long gap between twins, much longer than before
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One twin can be born as much as three months after the other

steps.title: A pregnant woman cannot conceive again
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: there is a rule that a pregnant woman cannot become pregnant a second time, so how can twins be three months apart?
steps.simpleTranslation: But the Master said: a woman does not become pregnant and then become pregnant again!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the three-month story. Such a big gap looks like two separate pregnancies, which the rule says cannot happen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A three-month gap suggests the second baby was conceived later, during the first pregnancy. A known rule says this never happens. So the גמרא asks how the story is possible.

keyTerms.meaning: But surely... (opens a challenge from a known rule)

phrases.english: But didn't the Master say:
A woman does not become pregnant
and then become pregnant again!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא אָמַר מָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the three-month report of step 10
steps.kashyaTarget: The story of twins born three months apart
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A three-month gap seems to need a second conception during the first pregnancy, which a known rule says cannot happen.

steps.title: One drop split into two
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that both twins came from one conception: one drop split in two, and the babies finished forming at different times.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: It was one drop that split into two. One baby's form was completed at the beginning of the seventh month, and the other at the end of the ninth.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי resolves the challenge. There was no second pregnancy, just one conception that grew into two babies at different speeds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both twins started together, so the rule against a second pregnancy is not broken. One was ready at the start of the seventh month and the other at the end of the ninth. That gap is about three months, which fits רב מנחם's story.

keyTerms.meaning: The beginning of the seventh month
The end of the ninth month

steps.whatToRemember: Twins can be born even three months apart. This is not two pregnancies but one conception that split, with each baby finishing at a different time.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
It was one drop
and it split into two.
The form of one was completed at the beginning of the seventh month
and the other at the end of the ninth.
phrases.notes: The words 'his form was completed' are left out here but understood from the line before.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: טִיפָּה אַחַת הָיְתָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 11
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case (one conception, not two)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A three-month gap means a second pregnancy
steps.terutzMaskana: One drop split in two; the babies were ready at the start of the seventh and the end of the ninth months

steps.title: An afterbirth in the house makes the house impure, according to רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line about an afterbirth in the house. Then it brings a ברייתא where רבי מאיר explains why the house is טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: if an afterbirth is in the house, the house is impure. The Rabbis taught: if an afterbirth is in the house, the house is impure. This is not because the afterbirth itself counts as a baby. It is because there is never an afterbirth without a baby inside it. This is the view of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא picks a new line from the משנה to discuss. It brings a ברייתא that explains רבי מאיר's reason for saying the house is טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר does not say the afterbirth is a baby. He says we assume a baby, or what is left of one, is inside it. That hidden baby is a dead body, so it gives טומאת אהל to everything under the roof.

keyTerms.meaning: Afterbirth, the sac that the baby grows in

steps.confusionAlert: רבי מאיר is NOT saying the afterbirth itself is a baby. The טומאה comes from the baby we assume is inside it.

phrases.english: An afterbirth in the house: the house is impure.
The Rabbis taught:
An afterbirth in the house: the house is impure,
not because the afterbirth is a baby,
but because there is no afterbirth
that has no baby with it,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.triggerLanguage: שִׁלְיָא בַּבַּיִת — הַבַּיִת טָמֵא. תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic. The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה about an afterbirth in the house.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An afterbirth in a house makes the house טמא, because we assume a baby is always inside it (רבי מאיר).

steps.title: Three sages say the house is pure
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי, רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון disagree with רבי מאיר and rule that the house is טהור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי, רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון say the house is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the other side of the מחלוקת: three sages say the house is טהור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These sages do not accept that the afterbirth in the house brings טומאה into it. The next steps show their argument against רבי מאיר.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei and Rabbi Yehuda
and Rabbi Shimon rule it pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מְטַהֲרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view in the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יוסי, רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון, an afterbirth in the house does not make the house טמא.

steps.title: The sages ask: you agree the outer room stays pure
steps.stepSummary: The sages point to a case where רבי מאיר himself agrees: if the afterbirth is carried in a basin to the outer room, that room is טהור.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to רבי מאיר: Don't you agree that if they carried it in a basin to the outer room, that room is pure?
steps.whatsHappening: The sages begin their argument by getting רבי מאיר to agree to a case. They are setting up a challenge to his view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a baby were always inside the afterbirth, the outer room should become טמא too. The sages want רבי מאיר to admit it is טהור, so they can use that against him.

phrases.english: They said to Rabbi Meir:
Don't you agree
that if they took it out in a basin
to the outer room, that it is pure?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר: אִי אַתָּה מוֹדֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The sages from step 14 start challenging רבי מאיר's view from step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי מאיר's rule that there is always a baby with the afterbirth
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a baby is always there, the outer room should also be טמא. Since רבי מאיר agrees it is טהור, his rule seems weak.

steps.title: רבי מאיר agrees: the baby is no longer there
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר agrees the outer room is טהור. He says this is because by then the baby has fallen apart and is gone.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: Yes. And why? Because the baby is no longer there.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר accepts the case but gives a reason that keeps his view in place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He agrees the outer room is טהור, but not because there was never a baby. While being moved, the baby fell apart and no longer exists. So his rule that the afterbirth always holds a baby still stands for the first room.

keyTerms.meaning: Because it is not there, it no longer exists

phrases.english: He said to them: Indeed.
phrases.notes: Here אבל does not mean 'but.' It means 'yes, I agree.'

phrases.english: And why? Because it is not there.
phrases.notes: He means the baby has fallen apart while being moved, so nothing is left of it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶן: אֲבָל. וְלָמָּה? לְפִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Agrees to the case but explains it with a different reason
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The outer room being טהור seemed to prove that there is no baby with the afterbirth.
steps.terutzMaskana: The outer room is טהור only because the baby fell apart on the way. That does not disprove that it was there to begin with.

steps.title: The sages push back: then it is gone from the inner room too
steps.stepSummary: The sages argue that if the baby fell apart before reaching the outer room, it also fell apart before reaching the inner room.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: Just as it is not there in the outer room, so too it is not there in the inner room!
steps.whatsHappening: The sages take רבי מאיר's own answer and turn it against him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If being moved makes the baby fall apart, then coming out of the mother into the first room is also a move. So the baby should already be gone in the inner room, and that room should be טהור too.

phrases.english: They said to him:
Just as it is not there in the outer room,
so too it is not there in the inner room!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁאֵינוֹ בַּבַּיִת הַחִיצוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי מאיר's answer from step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי מאיר's reason that the baby fell apart during the move
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same reasoning applies to the first move into the inner room, so the inner room should also be טהור.

steps.title: Falling apart once is not like falling apart twice
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר answers that a baby that broke down once may still be there, but one that broke down twice is surely gone.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: Something that fell apart once is not the same as something that fell apart twice.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר defends his view by showing a difference between the two rooms.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the inner room the baby has been moved only once, so something of it is still there and gives טומאה. Carrying it again to the outer room breaks it down a second time, and then nothing is left. So the inner room is טמא and the outer room is טהור.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not the same as

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר: inner room טמא (baby broke down once, still there). Outer room טהור (baby broke down twice, gone). The other sages: both rooms are טהור.

phrases.english: He said to them: It is not the same,
something that fell apart once,
as something that fell apart twice.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶן: אֵינוֹ דּוֹמֶה נִמּוֹק פַּעַם אַחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 17 and closes the debate in the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points out a difference between the two cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the baby falls apart when moved, it should be gone already in the inner room.
steps.terutzMaskana: One breakdown leaves something of the baby. A second breakdown leaves nothing.

steps.title: What is רבי שמעון's reason?
steps.stepSummary: A scene in the study hall: while sitting before רב המנונא, someone asks why רבי שמעון rules the house טהור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא sat behind רב ביבי in front of רב המנונא. He sat and said: What is the reason of רבי שמעון?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets the scene and asks for the reason behind רבי שמעון's view. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא told us רבי שמעון says טהור but did not say why. Now the גמרא looks for his reason, which may be different from the other sages' argument about the baby falling apart.

keyTerms.meaning: In front of him, before him

phrases.aramaic: יָתֵיב רַב פָּפָּא אֲחוֹרֵי דְּרַב בִּיבִי
phrases.english: Rav Pappa sat behind Rav Beivai
in front of Rav Hamnuna,
and he sat and was saying:
What is the reason of Rabbi Shimon?

steps.triggerLanguage: יָתֵיב רַב פָּפָּא אֲחוֹרֵי דְּרַב בִּיבִי קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב הַמְנוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to רבי שמעון from step 14 to find his reason.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why does רבי שמעון rule that a house with an afterbirth in it is טהור?

steps.title: רבי שמעון holds that impurity mixed with another kind is cancelled
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון holds that any טומאה mixed with a different kind of material is בטל. So the broken-down baby is cancelled out.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds that any impurity that got mixed with a different kind of material is cancelled.
steps.whatsHappening: The answer: רבי שמעון has a general rule that mixed טומאה gets cancelled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if remains of the baby are there, they are mixed with other material (the blood of the birth), which is a different kind. According to רבי שמעון, that mixture cancels the טומאה, so the house stays טהור.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds, he is of the opinion
It is cancelled, it loses its status

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows רבי שמעון's reason comes from a general rule about mixtures. It is a different reason from the debate about how many times the baby fell apart.

phrases.english: He holds that any impurity
that something of a different kind got mixed into is cancelled.
phrases.notes: Here the 'different kind' is the other material that comes out at birth, which mixes with the broken-down baby.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָסָבַר כׇּל טוּמְאָה שֶׁנִּתְעָרֵב בָּהּ מִמִּין אַחֵר בְּטֵלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי שמעון holds that טומאה mixed with a different kind of material is בטל, so the remains of the baby do not make the house טמא.

steps.title: רב פפא says the same reason applies to two more sages
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says that רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי rule the house טהור for the same reason as רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to them: This is also the reason of רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא adds one comment to the answer from Step 20: the same reason explains the view of רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 20 explained רבי שמעון: the baby is mixed with a different material and becomes בטל. רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי reach the same ruling as רבי שמעון, so רב פפא says their reason is the same. He adds no new law, only a link between the opinions.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to them:
phrases.notes: "Them" means רב ביבי and their teacher רב המנונא, from Step 19.

phrases.english: This is also the reason
of Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Yosei.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ רַב פָּפָּא: הַיְינוּ נָמֵי טַעְמַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the reason given in Step 20 to two other sages who rule the same way.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי rule טהור for the same reason as רבי שמעון: the mixed-in טומאה is בטל.

steps.title: The others laugh because the point is obvious
steps.stepSummary: The listeners laugh at רב פפא and say his point is obvious, since those sages hold the same ruling as רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: They laughed at him: What is different? It is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The others mock רב פפא's comment. They say there was no need to say it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their challenge is not about whether he is right. It is about whether his point adds anything. If two sages hold the same ruling as רבי שמעון, of course their reason is the same.

phrases.english: They laughed at him,
What is different? It is obvious!
phrases.notes: They mean: why would those two sages have any other reason? Saying so adds nothing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַחִיכוּ עֲלֵיהּ, מַאי שְׁנָא? פְּשִׁיטָא!
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for רב פפא's comment in Step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's statement that רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי share רבי שמעון's reason.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Since they hold the same ruling, sharing the same reason is obvious, so his point adds nothing.

steps.title: רב פפא's lesson: don't stay silent before your teacher
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא teaches that a person should say even an obvious point in front of his teacher, and he brings a פסוק from משלי to support this.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: A person should say even a matter like this, and not stay silent in front of his teacher, because it says: "If you acted foolishly, you will be lifted up, and if you muzzled yourself, your hand will be on your mouth."
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא draws a life lesson from being laughed at: speak up in learning, even if it might sound obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads the פסוק as a contrast. Someone who is willing to look foolish in learning will be lifted up. Someone who holds back from embarrassment will end up with his hand over his mouth, unable to answer.
steps.whatToRemember: Speaking up in learning is worthwhile even if others may laugh. Staying silent from embarrassment leaves a person unable to answer later.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a well-known lesson about how to learn: not being afraid to ask or say something in front of a teacher.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
Even a matter like this one
a person should say,
and he should not be silent in front of his teacher,
because it is said:
"If you acted foolishly, you will be lifted up,
phrases.notes: משלי 30:32. רב פפא reads it this way: being willing to look foolish in learning leads to being raised up.

phrases.english: and if you muzzled yourself, a hand on the mouth."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: אֲפִילּוּ כִּי הָא מִילְּתָא לֵימָא אִינִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the laughter in Step 22 with a teaching about learning.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A student should say even an obvious point before his teacher rather than stay silent.

steps.title: רבי שמעון holds the same idea about corpse-dust mixed with dirt
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that רבי שמעון is consistent. In a ברייתא, he rules that a ladleful of רקב with a little dirt mixed in is טהור.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי שמעון follows his own reasoning, as it is taught: A full ladle of corpse-dust that any amount of dirt fell into is impure, and רבי שמעון rules it pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to רבי שמעון. It brings another ברייתא to show he always holds that mixed-in טומאה can be cancelled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מלא תרווד of רקב is the minimum amount of corpse-dust that makes a house טמא. The other sages say a little dirt mixed in changes nothing. רבי שמעון says it is טהור, which matches his view in Step 20 that טומאה mixed with a different material is בטל.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon follows his own reasoning,
as it is taught:
A full ladle of corpse-dust
phrases.notes: This is the smallest amount of corpse-dust that makes a house טמא.

phrases.english: that any amount of ordinary dirt fell into —
is impure,
and Rabbi Shimon rules it pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַזְדָּא רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן לְטַעְמֵיהּ, דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to רבי שמעון's reason from Step 20 and shows he holds it in another case.
steps.raayaObject: רבי שמעון consistently holds that טומאה mixed with a different material can be cancelled.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about a ladleful of רקב with dirt mixed in, which רבי שמעון rules טהור.

steps.title: Why does רבי שמעון rule the corpse-dust pure?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רבי שמעון's ruling in the ladleful case.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of רבי שמעון?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how a full ladleful of רקב can become טהור just because a little dirt fell in. It is setting up רבה's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The full measure of corpse-dust is still there, and only a bit of dirt was added. So the גמרא needs to explain how the amount stops counting.

phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi Shimon?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the ruling quoted in Step 24.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why a full ladleful of רקב becomes טהור when any amount of dirt is mixed in.

steps.title: Two grains of dirt cancel one grain of corpse-dust
steps.stepSummary: רבה reports what he heard in the study hall: somewhere in the mix, two grains of dirt will outnumber one grain of רקב and cancel it, so less than a full ladleful remains.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: I found the Sages of the study hall of רב sitting and saying: It is impossible that there won't be two grains of dirt outnumbering one grain of corpse-dust, and so the measure is lacking.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers the question by quoting the sages of רב's study hall. Somewhere in the mixture, the dirt outnumbers a grain of רקב and cancels it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In some spot of the mixture, two grains of dirt will surround one grain of רקב. That grain is בטל to the majority. Once even one grain is cancelled, the רקב is less than a full ladleful, so it is too small to make the house טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: it is lacking (below the required amount)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי שמעון: when a full ladleful of רקב is mixed with dirt, one grain is surely cancelled by the dirt. Then the measure is incomplete, so it is טהור.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי שמעון does not say the whole ladleful is cancelled. Only one grain needs to be cancelled to drop it below the minimum amount.

phrases.english: Rabba said:
I found the Sages of the study hall of Rav
sitting and saying:
It is impossible that there will not be more
two grains of dirt
than one grain of corpse-dust,
phrases.notes: He means that in some spot of the mixture, the dirt outnumbers a grain of רקב and cancels it.

phrases.english: and so it is lacking.
phrases.notes: The full ladleful is now missing that one cancelled grain, so it is below the minimum amount.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה: אַשְׁכַּחְתִּינְהוּ לְרַבָּנַן דְּבֵי רַב דְּיָתְבִי וְקָאָמְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Two grains of dirt will outnumber and cancel one grain of רקב somewhere in the mix. This leaves less than a full ladleful, which is not enough to make the house טמא.

steps.title: רבה answers 'on the contrary' to the study-hall reason
steps.stepSummary: רבה tells the study hall that their reasoning works the other way. It is impossible that two grains of רקב will not outnumber a grain of dirt.
steps.simpleTranslation: And I said to them: On the contrary! It is impossible that two grains of רקב will not outnumber [one grain of dirt]...
steps.whatsHappening: רבה tells us how he challenged the reason he heard in the study hall. He flips their logic around, and the sentence finishes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The study hall said the dirt cancels some of the רקב, so less than a full ladleful remains and it is טהור. רבה says you can just as easily say the רקב, which is the bigger part of the mix, outnumbers and cancels the dirt. If so, it should all count as רקב and be a full ladleful, which would make it טמא, the opposite of רבי שמעון's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: On the contrary; the reverse is true
Decayed flesh of a dead body, which can make things טמא in the amount of a ladleful

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two sides. The study hall said dirt cancels רקב. רבה says the opposite: רקב cancels dirt.

phrases.english: And I said to them: On the contrary,
phrases.notes: רבה is still talking. 'Them' are the people in the study hall whose reason he just reported.

phrases.english: it is impossible that there will not be more
two grains of רקב over
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud. It says the two grains of רקב outnumber one grain of dirt.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמֵינָא לְהוּ: אַדְּרַבָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason given in Step 26 by applying the same logic in the opposite direction.
steps.kashyaTarget: The study-hall reason that two grains of dirt cancel one grain of רקב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Canceling by majority can work both ways. Since there is more רקב than dirt, the רקב should cancel the dirt, which would leave a full ladleful that is טמא.
